title: One Model to Dose Them All: A Population Pharmacokinetic Model for Multiple Aminoglycosides Across the Human Lifespan

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: (a) Available data were split into 70% training and 30% test sets. (b) Training data were available across three drugs (amikacin, gentamicin, and tobramycin) and three age groups (neonates, children, and adults). The Unified model was trained on all available data; leave‐one‐out models were trained on all but one of the drug‐age groups; and single drug models were trained only on one drug. (c) Leave‐one‐out models were evaluated against the Unified model on the excluded drug–age pair. Single drug models were evaluated against the Unified model on the single drug, and on the other two drugs. The Unified model was also evaluated against published models on the entire test dataset.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Accuracy, mean percent error (MPE), and normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) of predictions for the newly fit model and published models on the test dataset for (a) neonatal patients (N = 1153 observations), (b) pediatric patients (N = 406), and (c) adult patients (N = 2569). The symbol ◂ indicates the best model; the symbol ◁ indicates models that are not statistically distinguishable from the best model. For each model, the drug the model was developed for is given first (T = tobramycin, A = amikacin, and G = gentamicin), followed by the author name. IllAdult and IllPNA refer to the Illamola model for adults and the Illamola model with postnatal age, respectively. Smit 19 and Smit 20 refer to reference [19] and Smit et al. 2020, 36 respectively.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Accuracy, mean percent error (MPE), and normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) of predictions for the newly fit model and the same model trained only on one drug, evaluated on only the included drug in the test dataset, in (a) neonates, (b) children, and (c) adults. For example, the single drug model trained with amikacin (“Single Drug”) is evaluated against the model with all training data (“Unified”) in the leftmost column (“ami only”). The symbol ◂ indicates the best model; the symbol ◁ indicates models that are not statistically distinguishable from the best model.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Accuracy, mean percent error (MPE), and normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) of predictions for the newly fit model and the same model trained only on one drug, evaluated on test data not from that drug, in (a) neonates, (b) children, and (c) adults. For example, the single drug model trained with amikacin (“Single Drug”) is evaluated against the model with all training data (“Unified”) in the leftmost column (“not ami”) on test data from gentamicin and tobramycin. The symbol ◂ indicates the best model; the symbol ◁ indicates models that are not statistically distinguishable from the best model.
